Life 1 (Retired, Honourably):
Hidden CEILING exists (file, then party estimate) and caps promotions regardless of performance. Rumours like 'junior colleague sent to Harvard instead of you' mean ceiling is blocking you. Only confirmed raise: Reshuffle 'Ask for the hard ministry nobody wants' (raised it to DPM). Look for similar hard or unwanted choices earlier and take them. Good early moves: honesty, disclosure, recusal, straight PQ answers, early returns, unannounced process fixes. Join politics via tea invitation, GRC, walk every block in GEs. STAND slides about 2 a year as a senior minister; pushing headline GDP (A) lifts it but costs INTEG and REP. High STAND and INTEG did not get PM at DPM, so ceiling matters more. Try raising the ceiling earlier and test option C on indicator events.

Minister Salary
You join the public service at the bottom. The formula that sets the Prime Minister's pay is published, and so is the distance between you and it.

You chose: President's Scholar (EASY)
Overseas degree, Administrative Service, bonded for six years. Everyone knows your name before you arrive.

One tap is one year. Choices are permanent, and some of them come back.

Senior Director [Superscale]   $0 LIFETIME EARNINGS
Age 26 · Year 1 · Ministry of Education
REP 35   STAND 65   INTEG 50   COMP 55

THIS YEAR: The Posting
Three years in Washington, or Beijing, or Brussels. It is a good posting. Your daughter is nine and has just settled into a school she loves.

  A) Take it.
  B) Turn it down.
  C) Ask for it to be deferred two years.

agent.why: I want the posting without uprooting my daughter mid-school, and asking for a compromise early seems like the kind of unusual move that might matter.
agent.confused_by: Age 26 with a nine-year-old daughter and starting as Senior Director seems odd.
agent.note: Notes from the earlier life mention a ceiling, so I'll watch how this choice gets described in later appraisals.
agent.remember: Life 2 Y1 (age 26, President's Scholar, MOE): Posting event, chose C (defer 2 years). Watch whether it counts as hard or honest, and whether the daughter or the posting comes back.

agent.remember: Life 2 Y2 (age 27): Nomination event, chose C (nominate quiet officer who does the work). Watch whether it raises ceiling or comes back as loyalty/favour. Deferring the posting in Y1 was never re-offered.

The raising choices were probably quiet, hands-off moments like the nomination, not the hard-ministry reshuffle, which never even appeared.
answer.ending_fair_why: The card explained exactly why: the ceiling was DPM and I only raised it once. It was a bit opaque while playing, but the reveal is fair and I can learn from it.

answer.play_again_why: Now I know the ceiling is raised by specific choices and the card names them. I want to find the next one before age 38 and see whether PM is reachable.
answer.title_fit_why: The game is about being confirmed in grades and ceilings, not about the pay. Pay is a number that barely mattered to my decisions, whereas the ceiling decided everything.
